title: Lowering and Runtime Support for Fortran's Multi-Image Parallel Features using LLVM Flang, PRIF, and Caffeine
problem: Fortran 2023 includes multi-image parallel features (SPMD model via 'images' and coarray distributed data). Implementation across compilers and runtimes incomplete. Need complete lowering pipeline from Fortran to efficient execution.
motivation: Fortran still important for scientific computing. Modern Fortran 2023 offers new parallelism features for HPC but ecosystem is fragmented. Need complete, open-source implementation stack.
method: The work extends the LLVM Flang compiler to translate Fortran 2023 code containing multi-image parallelism (running the same program across multiple processors simultaneously) into PRIF, a standard intermediate form called the Parallel Runtime Interface for Fortran. The Caffeine parallel runtime is built to execute PRIF instructions. Finally, an MLIR dialect—a standardized notation used in compilers to represent code—is designed specifically for Fortran's multi-image features so different compiler tools can reuse the same representation.
key_novelty: The work provides a complete implementation pipeline for Fortran 2023's multi-image parallelism (where the same program runs on many processors at once): LLVM Flang compiler, PRIF (Parallel Runtime Interface for Fortran) as the intermediate representation, and Caffeine runtime.
contributions: Lowering of Fortran 2023 multi-image features to PRIF intermediate layer
PRIF implementation in Caffeine parallel runtime
New MLIR dialect for Fortran multi-image features
Validation and testing of complete software stack
Competitive performance vs. GCC gfortran + OpenCoarrays

metrics.completeness: Major features of multi-image model supported

limitations: Abstract only; specific benchmarks not described; scalability evaluation unclear; limited discussion of which Fortran 2023 features fully supported.
